newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX continues falling on flat trade.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX continues falling on flat trade.

text.p: The Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) opened the week with a quiet session on Monday, as the SAX index closed lower on losses to steel maker VSZ.
The 16-share SAX index closed down 1.59 points at 183.99.

VSZ closed down 30 crowns at 620 and brokers said the bourse should continue to fall, mainly on investors expecting a devaluation of the Slovak crown after its turbulent development over the last month.

"Those who expected the crown to be devalued, have left the market. In my opinion, they are now waiting for prices of shares to fall, which would have a devaluation effect," said Bohus Betko of ING Barings.
"But a real disaster would be if prices fall and the crown will devalue later anyway, making the shares only pieces of paper," Betko added.
Overall, volume increased to 712,903 shares, from 376,910 shares traded on Friday, while turnover rose to 590.07 million crowns, from 338.07 million.
